problem: A gardener has 60 litres of rainwater in a big barrel and pours it evenly into 10 watering cans. How many litres end up in each watering can?
How much juice goes into each jug? At the school picnic, the cook shares 60 litres of orange juice equally among 10 jugs.
Kofi has a block of clay that weighs 96 ounces. He cuts it into 4 equal chunks and then splits every chunk into 3 equal balls. What does one ball of clay weigh?
follow_up_questions: He presses 2 of the balls together to make a small bowl. How much clay is in the bowl?
He sticks a 7-ounce clay handle onto the bowl. What is the weight of the finished bowl?

problem: What does each candle weigh? Mirela melts 96 ounces of wax and pours it into 4 molds of equal size; later she slices every molded block into 3 equal candles.
follow_up_questions: She ties 2 of the candles together as a gift. How much wax is in the gift?
A glass holder weighing 7 ounces is added to the gift. What does the gift weigh now?

problem: After the school fair, 20 litres of lemonade are left over, and the 5 teachers who ran the stand share them equally. How many litres does each teacher take?
follow_up_questions: Each teacher pours the lemonade into bottles that hold 2 litres. How many bottles does one teacher fill?
How many bottles do all the teachers fill altogether?
Every bottle gets 3 ice cubes. How many ice cubes are needed?

problem: How many kilograms of rice does each cook get when a camp kitchen splits its last 20 kilograms of rice equally among 5 cooks at the end of the season?
follow_up_questions: Each cook packs the rice into bags of 2 kilograms. How many bags does one cook pack?
What is the number of bags packed by all the cooks?
Every bag gets 3 labels. How many labels are needed in total?

problem: Rosa has 40 ounces of birdseed and fills 8 feeders with the same amount. Her garden has 13 kinds of birds. How much seed goes in each feeder?
follow_up_questions: She adds 3 ounces of sunflower seeds to every feeder. How much does one feeder hold now?
Her neighbour fills 4 feeders exactly like that. How much seed do those feeders hold altogether?

problem: How much wax goes into each candle jar? A candle maker, whose shop has 13 shelves, pours 40 ounces of wax equally into 8 jars.
follow_up_questions: Each jar also gets a 3-ounce lid. What do one candle and its lid weigh?
A customer buys 4 of these candles with lids. What do they weigh in all?

problem: Coach Diaz has 21 metres of rope to make 3 jump ropes of equal length. The rope is striped red and blue. How long is each jump rope?
follow_up_questions: One child wants a rope 2 metres longer than the others. How long would that rope be?

problem: What length of ribbon does each gift get? Tomasz cuts 21 metres of ribbon into equal pieces for 3 gifts. His sister wraps the boxes in gold paper.
follow_up_questions: The biggest gift needs 2 metres more ribbon than planned. How much ribbon does it get?

problem: A school has two hallways, one 48 metres long and one 33 metres long. The janitors split their total length into 9 equal parts, one part for each janitor. How many metres does each janitor mop?
follow_up_questions: Mopping one metre takes 4 minutes. How long does each janitor mop for?
How many minutes do all the janitors mop altogether?

problem: How long is each painter's section? Two fences, 48 metres and 33 metres long, are being painted by 9 painters, who divide the combined length equally.
follow_up_questions: A painter needs 4 minutes for each metre. How many minutes does one painter work?
Add up the minutes for every painter. What is the total?

problem: A bottle of food colouring holds 30 mL, enough for 6 cake batches using equal amounts. The bottle cost 18 dollars. How many millilitres does each batch get?
follow_up_questions: Chef Amina bakes only 2 of the batches today. How much colouring does she use?
How much colouring is left in the bottle?
Each batch also needs 9 mL of vanilla. How much vanilla will the batches she has not baked yet need?

problem: How many millilitres of paint will each painting group get? An art teacher has a 30 mL tube of blue paint, planned to be split equally among 6 groups. The tube came in a box of 18.
follow_up_questions: Only 2 of the groups paint this morning. How much paint do they use?
How much paint is left in the tube?
Each group also needs 9 mL of white paint. How much white paint will the groups still waiting need?

problem: A 75 cm long window box is split into 5 equal parts, one for each kind of herb. How wide is each part?
follow_up_questions: The basil plants fill 9 cm of their part. How much of that part is still empty?

problem: What is the length of each section of the coat rack? The rack in the school hallway measures 75 cm and is divided into 5 equal sections.
follow_up_questions: One child's coat covers 9 cm of a section. How many centimetres of that section are free?

problem: At the school fair, Mr. Haddad sold 18 litres of iced tea in 6 hours, selling the same amount every hour. How many litres did he sell each hour?
follow_up_questions: One litre fills 4 glasses. How many glasses did he sell in an hour?
A glass costs 2 dollars. How much money did he collect each hour?

problem: How many litres of soup did the food truck serve per hour? It was parked at the beach for 6 hours and served 18 litres in total, the same amount each hour.
follow_up_questions: Every litre makes 4 bowls. How many bowls were served each hour?
Each bowl sells for 2 dollars. What were the truck's takings in one hour?

problem: A zookeeper divides 40 pounds of fish equally among 5 penguin buckets. The oldest penguin is 11 years old. How many pounds of fish are in each bucket?
follow_up_questions: She tops up every bucket with 4 more pounds of fish. How many pounds of fish does each bucket hold now?
How many pounds of fish are in all the buckets together?

problem: How many ounces of popcorn are in each bowl? At a sleepover for 11 friends, Dad pours 40 ounces of popcorn evenly into 5 big bowls.
follow_up_questions: He adds 4 ounces of pretzels to each bowl. What is the weight of snacks in one bowl?
What do the snacks in all the bowls weigh together?

problem: Two rain barrels in Mr. Petrov's garden hold 45 litres and 39 litres. He empties both into 7 watering cans, the same amount in each. How many litres does each can hold?
How many cups of punch go into each pitcher? For the class party, the teacher mixes a 45-cup batch and a 39-cup batch, then pours it all evenly into 7 pitchers.
A ferry captain sailed 63 km in 7 crossings, each the same distance. Seagulls followed the boat all day. How long is one crossing?
follow_up_questions: Tomorrow the captain makes 4 crossings. How far will the ferry sail?

problem: How far did the school bus travel on each run if it covered 63 km in 7 runs of equal length? Its windows were very dusty.
follow_up_questions: On Monday the bus makes 4 of these runs. What distance does it travel?

problem: Sana spends 56 minutes knitting 8 squares for a blanket, the same time on every square. How long does one square take her?
follow_up_questions: Her brother Omar needs 2 more minutes per square than Sana. How long does one square take Omar?
Omar knits 5 squares. How many minutes does that take him?
How many more minutes did Sana knit than Omar?

problem: How many minutes does Pedro spend on each page? He takes 56 minutes to colour a comic of 8 pages, spending equal time on each one.
follow_up_questions: His friend Lin is slower by 2 minutes on every page. How long does Lin take for a page?
Lin colours 5 pages. How many minutes does she spend?
Find how much longer Pedro coloured than Lin.

problem: A music teacher splits a 36-minute lesson equally among 6 students so each gets a solo turn. How many minutes does each student play?
How long does each child get on the climbing wall? The gym gives a group of 6 children 36 minutes on the wall, shared equally.
Yuki gathered 49 ounces of blueberries and her grandfather gathered 41 ounces. They mix the berries together and fill 6 jars equally. How many ounces go in each jar?
follow_up_questions: The berries in each jar are split into 3 equal pies. How many ounces of berries are in each pie?
How many pies are there altogether?

problem: What does each loaf weigh? Bakers Ola and Finn make 49 ounces and 41 ounces of dough, combine it, and shape it into 6 loaves of equal weight.
follow_up_questions: Each loaf is sliced into 3 equal chunks. What does one chunk weigh?
How many chunks are there in total?

problem: A gardener planted 24 feet of hedge in 4 equal rows along the path. The hedge has tiny white flowers. How long is each row?
follow_up_questions: She plants one more row of the same length. How many feet of hedge are there now?

problem: How long is each banner strip? For the parade, Rafael hangs 24 feet of banner in 4 equal strips. The crowd cheered loudly.
follow_up_questions: He hangs one extra strip just as long. What length of banner is up now?

problem: A farmer picks 45 pounds of apples and spreads them evenly across 5 crates at her stand. How many pounds of apples are in each crate?
follow_up_questions: A customer buys 4 pounds from one crate. How many pounds stay in that crate?
How many pounds of apples are left at the stand in all?
Later, 21 more pounds are sold. How many pounds are left?

problem: How many pounds of potatoes does each sack hold? The school cook has 45 pounds of potatoes and 5 sacks, and she puts the same weight in each sack.
follow_up_questions: She uses 4 pounds from one sack for lunch. How many pounds remain in that sack?
What weight of potatoes is left in all the sacks together?
By Friday she uses another 21 pounds. What weight remains?

problem: Before 6 o'clock, Dmitri divides 64 ounces of trail mix into 8 bags of equal weight for his hiking group. What does one bag weigh?
follow_up_questions: His friend takes 3 bags. How many ounces of trail mix does the friend take?
Dmitri then mixes another 16 ounces and adds it to what he kept. How many ounces of trail mix does he have now?

problem: What weight of coffee beans goes into each tin? Lucia opens her coffee cart, which has 6 stools, with 64 ounces of beans and splits them evenly into 8 tins.
follow_up_questions: A cafe owner buys 3 tins. What weight of beans does she buy?
Lucia roasts 16 more ounces and adds them to what she has left. How many ounces of beans does she have now?

problem: A florist shares 27 roses equally among 9 vases for a wedding. How many roses go in each vase?
Find how many crayons land on each desk. The art teacher has 27 crayons and gives the same number to each of the 9 desks.
A farm sent 15 litres of milk to a summer camp and split it equally among 5 cabins. The cabins have green roofs. How many litres did each cabin get?
follow_up_questions: The farm sends the same amount again the next day. How many litres did it send over both days?

problem: How much water did each team get? The coach filled a cooler with 15 litres and shared it equally among 5 teams at the field day. The sun was very hot.
follow_up_questions: On the second field day, the coach brings the same amount again. How much water is that for the two days?

problem: A carpenter has a 96 cm wooden board. He saws it into 8 equal lengths and then cuts each length in half. How long is each small piece?
follow_up_questions: He uses 10 small pieces to build a birdhouse. What length of board does the birdhouse use?
How much of the board's length is left over?

problem: How long is each short ribbon? Mia cuts a 96 cm ribbon into 8 equal parts, then halves every part.
follow_up_questions: She ties 10 of the short ribbons onto a kite tail. How much ribbon is on the kite?
What length of the original ribbon is not on the kite?

problem: A loop of the playground track is 25 metres. Over 6 training days, Zara ran 48 loops, the same number each day. How many loops did she run per day?
follow_up_questions: Each loop is 25 metres. How far did Zara run on one training day?
Her brother ran 3 loops fewer than Zara each day. How far did he run in one day?
How much farther did Zara run than her brother on one day?

problem: How many lengths did Omar row at each session? The canal stretch is 25 metres long, and Omar rowed 48 lengths over 6 sessions, the same number every session.
follow_up_questions: One length is 25 metres. What distance did Omar row in a session?
His cousin rowed 3 lengths fewer per session. What distance did the cousin row in one session?
By how many metres did Omar out-row his cousin in one session?

problem: A builder has 56 kg of sand and 49 kg of gravel. He mixes them and shares the mix equally among 7 big planters for a park. How many kilograms go in each planter?
How many kilograms of feed does each pen get? Farmer Okeke has 56 kg of corn and 49 kg of oats, and he spreads all of it equally over his 7 chicken pens.
The music class lasts 45 minutes, and the teacher plays 3 songs of equal length. How many minutes long is each song?
follow_up_questions: Next time she plays 5 songs in the same total time. How long can each song be?
How many minutes shorter is each song than before?

problem: How long is each game? During gym, 45 minutes are split into 3 games of the same length.
follow_up_questions: Tomorrow the coach squeezes 5 games into the same amount of time. How long will each game last?
By how many minutes is a game shorter tomorrow than today?

problem: Tariq paid $24 for 6 bus tickets, all costing the same. How much was one ticket?
What is the price of one pencil case if a teacher buys 6 identical ones for $24?
Three sisters sold handmade bracelets at the market and made $27. Their table had 2 baskets on it. Sharing the money equally, how much does each sister get?
follow_up_questions: One sister spends $4 on a hair clip. How much money does she keep?
The next market day they make twice as much. How much is each sister's share then?

problem: How much money does each of the three brothers get? They raked leaves on Sunday, filled 2 trailers, and earned $27 to split evenly.
follow_up_questions: The youngest spends $4 on a yo-yo. What is left of his share?
The following Sunday they earn twice as much. What is each brother's share that day?

problem: The art club sold 14 paintings for $6 each and shared all the money equally among its 4 teams. How much money did each team get?
follow_up_questions: Each team spends $15 on brushes. How much does one team have left?
Two teams put their leftover money together. How much do they have?
They want a $30 easel. How much more money do they need?

problem: How much does each patrol receive? The scouts sold 14 boxes of cookies at $6 a box, and the money was split equally among 4 patrols.
follow_up_questions: A patrol spends $15 on a set of tent pegs. What money does it have left?
Two patrols pool their leftovers. How much money is that?
What more do they need for a $30 lantern?

problem: Mrs. Tanaka paid $45 for zoo tickets for her group of 5, each ticket the same price. The zoo had a new baby giraffe. How much did one ticket cost?
follow_up_questions: Next year each ticket will cost $3 more. What will one ticket cost?

problem: What was the price of each train ticket? The 5 members of the Garcia family travelled to the coast and paid $45 in all for tickets that each cost the same. The train had a dining car.
follow_up_questions: In winter the fare rises by $3 per ticket. What will one ticket cost then?

problem: The book fair raised $56, and the money is split equally among 8 classes for new library books. What is each class's share?
follow_up_questions: One class adds $9 from a class jar. How much money does that class have now?
Books cost $4 each. How many books can that class buy?

problem: Find each team's share: the sports day raffle made $56, divided evenly among 8 teams to buy equipment.
follow_up_questions: One team adds $9 of its own. What is its total now?
Jump ropes cost $4 each. How many jump ropes can that team buy?

problem: Five neighbours gave equal amounts to collect $40 for a new park bench. The park has 3 fountains. How much did each neighbour give?
follow_up_questions: Later each neighbour doubles the gift. How much has one neighbour given altogether?

problem: How much did each of the 5 classes donate? Together the classes gave $40 for a new class pet, each giving the same amount, and the school already has 3 hamsters.
follow_up_questions: Later every class doubles its donation. How much has one class given in total?

problem: Amira saved the same amount each week for 6 weeks to buy a $42 tent. How much did she save per week?
follow_up_questions: A sleeping bag costs $21. How many weeks of saving will it take to pay for it?
What do the tent and the sleeping bag cost together?

problem: What did Luca save each week? His new guitar cost $42, and he paid for it by saving an equal sum for 6 weeks.
follow_up_questions: A guitar case costs $21. How many weeks of saving does the case take?
Find the total cost of the guitar and the case.

problem: Ines and her two brothers walked dogs on Saturday. They earned $15 from one neighbour and $24 from another and shared it all equally. How much did each of the 3 children get?
follow_up_questions: Ines spends $5 on a sandwich. How much of her share is left?
Both brothers keep all of their money. How much do the three children have altogether now?
They want to buy a $60 tent. How much more money do they need?

problem: How much money did each of the 3 friends receive? Kwame, Lior and Pia washed windows, earning $15 at the bakery and $24 at the bookshop, and split the total evenly.
follow_up_questions: Kwame buys a $5 snack. What remains of his share?
Both of the others save every dollar. What do the three friends have together now?
Their goal is a $60 telescope. How much are they still short?

problem: It was too windy to play outside, so Theo's aunt took him and three cousins bowling. She bought 32 game tickets for the 4 children to share equally. The bowling balls were bright pink. How many tickets did each child get?
follow_up_questions: A game of air hockey costs 2 tickets. How many games can one child play?

problem: How many stickers did each child receive? Grandpa shared 32 stickers evenly among the 4 kids at the library. The library had a big fish tank.
follow_up_questions: Each page of a sticker book holds 2 stickers. How many pages can one child fill?

problem: A pack of 9 puzzle books costs $63 in total. What does one book cost?
What is the price of one model rocket if nine of them cost the science club $63 altogether?
The chess team won $80 at a tournament and shared it evenly among its 8 players. The final game lasted 4 rounds. How much did each player get?
follow_up_questions: Nadia wants a $25 chess clock. How much more money does she need?
She also wants a $6 chess book. How much do the clock and the book cost together?

problem: How much did each singer receive? A choir of 8 singers won $80 in a contest and split it equally; they had sung 4 songs.
follow_up_questions: One singer is saving for a $25 microphone. How much more does she need after using her share?
A $6 cable is needed too. What do the microphone and the cable cost together?

problem: Jonas baked 24 cookies and laid them out on 3 plates, the same number on every plate. How many cookies were on each plate?
follow_up_questions: He sold each cookie for $2. How much money did one plate bring in?
What did all the plates bring in together?
He had spent $18 on flour and butter. How much profit did he make?

problem: How many seedlings are in each tray? Aunt Rosa potted 24 tomato seedlings and set them in 3 trays with equal numbers.
follow_up_questions: She sells the seedlings for $2 apiece. What does one full tray earn?
What do all the trays earn together?
Soil and pots cost her $18. What is her profit?

problem: Leaves were piled high in every yard. Five friends earned $35 raking leaves and split it evenly. How much did each friend get?
follow_up_questions: Then a neighbour gave each friend a $3 tip. How much does one friend have now?
How much do all the friends have together now?

problem: How much did each dancer receive when 5 dancers shared $35 from their street show equally? Music filled the whole square.
follow_up_questions: A passer-by then gave each dancer $3 more. What does one dancer have now?
What do the dancers have altogether?

problem: The garden club made $46 selling plants and $38 selling seeds. All the money was shared equally among 4 school gardens. How much did each garden get?
What did each of the 4 grades receive? A book swap raised $46 on Friday and $38 on Saturday, and the total was split evenly among the grades.
Seven classmates paid equal amounts for a $21 pizza. How much did each classmate pay?
follow_up_questions: They order a second pizza and share the cost the same way. How much has each classmate paid in all?

problem: What was each cousin's part? A $21 board game was bought by 7 cousins, and each of them put in the same amount.
follow_up_questions: Then they buy another game at the same price and pay the same way. What has each cousin spent in total?

problem: The library club had $75 in the bank and raised $21 more at a book sale. It split all the money equally among 8 new shelves. How much was set aside for each shelf?
follow_up_questions: One shelf cost only $9. How much of its share was left?
Five shelves each have that much left. How much is that altogether?

problem: How much money did each classroom get? A school had $75 saved, collected $21 more at a car boot sale, and shared everything equally among its 8 classrooms.
follow_up_questions: Classroom A spent only $9 of its share. How much is left over?
If 5 classrooms each have that much left, what is the total?

problem: On a hot day, Rania and Lotte sold ice pops by the pool. They made $18 and shared it evenly between the two of them. How much did each girl get?
What was each boy's share? Twins Arjun and Dev earned $18 walking dogs and split it equally between the two of them.
The 5 Haddad children went to the toy fair, which had 40 stalls, and their mother gave them $30 to share equally. How much did each child get?
follow_up_questions: Samir Haddad buys a $4 puzzle. How much does he have left?
His uncle gives him $5 more. How much does Samir have now?

problem: How much spending money did each child get? At the zoo, 5 children were given $30 by their teacher to share equally, and the zoo had 40 kinds of birds.
follow_up_questions: Mila spends $4 on a postcard. What is left of her money?
A friend pays her back $5. What does Mila have now?

problem: A science teacher bought 36 test tubes and set them evenly into 4 racks, one rack for each lab table. The lab has a big window. How many test tubes are in each rack?
follow_up_questions: Each table uses 6 test tubes from its rack. How many are left unused in each rack?

problem: How many seed packets went into each box? The garden club got 36 packets and divided them equally into 4 boxes, one per flower bed. The boxes have pictures of bees on them.
follow_up_questions: Each bed uses 6 packets from its box. How many packets are left in each box?

problem: Uncle Teo gave his 4 nieces $20 to split equally at the fair. How much did each niece get?
follow_up_questions: A ride costs $3. How much does each niece have after one ride?
The nieces put their leftover money together. How much do they have?

problem: How much money did each girl get? A coach handed $20 to 4 girls on the team to share evenly at the snack bar.
follow_up_questions: Each girl buys a $3 smoothie. How much money does each girl have left?
Together, how much leftover money do the girls have?

problem: Kenji earned $92 mowing lawns over 4 weekends, the same amount each weekend. How much did he earn per weekend?
What did the bake stall make each weekend? Over 4 weekends it took in $92, with every weekend bringing the same amount.
Six children sold raffle tickets for the school library, each collecting the same amount, $54 in all. The raffle ran for 3 days. How much did each child collect?
follow_up_questions: A local shop doubles each child's amount. What does one child's amount become?

problem: How much money did each of the 6 runners raise? In a 3 km charity run the runners raised $54 altogether, each raising the same.
follow_up_questions: A company doubles what each runner raised. What is one runner's amount now?

problem: A puppet troupe of 4 performers earned $48 at a birthday party and split it evenly. How much did each performer earn?
follow_up_questions: One performer spends $5 on new puppet eyes. How much does she keep?
Two of the other performers spend nothing. What do those two have together?

problem: What did each of the 4 painters earn? Together they were paid $48 for painting a fence, divided equally.
follow_up_questions: One painter buys a $5 brush. How much money does he have left?
Two of the others save all their pay. How much do those two have between them?

problem: Gabriel used a $36 voucher to pay for swimming pool entry for four people, all at the same price. The pool had a twisty slide. How much was each entry?
follow_up_questions: Towels cost $5 per person. How much did the towels for the group cost?

problem: How much did one museum ticket cost? Hana's $36 gift card covered tickets for 4 people, each costing the same. The museum had a huge dinosaur skeleton.
follow_up_questions: Audio guides are $5 each, and everyone gets one. How much do the audio guides for the group cost?

problem: Sixteen campers split into 4 equal groups for a canoe race. How many campers are in each group?
How many players are on each team when 16 children at the park form 4 teams of the same size?
A piano teacher charges $72 for 8 lessons, each at the same price. Her student Mina has played for 10 months. How much is one lesson?
follow_up_questions: Mina takes 3 lessons this month. How much does she pay?
She pays with a $50 note. How much change does she get?

problem: How much does one swim lesson cost? The pool sells a block of 8 lessons for $72, all priced the same, and it has 10 lanes.
follow_up_questions: Leo's dad books 3 lessons. What does he pay?
He hands over a $50 note. What change comes back?

problem: At the farm, 12 families paid $96 altogether for hayrides, each family paying the same. How much did one family pay?
follow_up_questions: Apple cider is $2 a cup, and each family buys 3 cups. What does a family spend on the hayride and the cider together?

problem: How much did each class pay? The museum charged 12 classes $96 in total for a guided tour, the same for every class.
follow_up_questions: Each class also buys 3 posters at $2 each. What does one class spend on the tour and the posters?

problem: Raj's family rode the go-karts 5 times at the fair, and the rides cost $35, each ride the same price. How much was one ride?
follow_up_questions: Helmets added $5 to the cost. What was the full cost?
Raj's mum paid with a $50 note. How much change did she get?
She splits the change equally between both of her children. How much does each child get?

problem: What is the cost of a single round of mini golf? The Kim family played 5 rounds and paid $35, every round costing the same.
follow_up_questions: Ball rental added $5 to the total. How much was the total then?
Mr. Kim paid with a $50 note. What change did he receive?
The change is shared evenly between both Kim children. What does each child receive?

problem: A science kit costs $13. The school orders 6 of them, and 3 teachers share the cost equally. How much does each teacher pay?
How much does each of the 3 aunts pay? They buy 6 jigsaw puzzles for the cousins at $13 each and split the bill evenly.
Chef Pablo split 45 meatballs equally among 9 plates. His menu lists 6 kinds of pasta. How many meatballs are on each plate?
follow_up_questions: Each meatball costs $2. What is the price of one plate?

problem: How many strawberries are in each cup? At the fruit stand, which has 6 baskets of lemons, Aiko divided 45 strawberries evenly into 9 cups.
follow_up_questions: Every strawberry costs $2. What does one cup cost?

problem: Ahmed, Bea and Carlos earned $21 selling comics and shared it equally among the three of them. How much did each one get?
follow_up_questions: Bea adds her share to the $15 already in her wallet. How much is in her wallet now?

problem: What is each cousin's share? Three cousins found $21 in their birthday cards and split it evenly.
follow_up_questions: One cousin puts her share in a jar that already has $15 in it. How much is in the jar now?

problem: Over two days, the class sold lemonade: 23 cups on Friday and 17 cups on Saturday, at $2 a cup. The money was shared equally among 4 class projects. How much did each project get?
follow_up_questions: The garden project spends $14 of its share. How much is left in the garden fund?
The reading project spends half of its share on books. How much do the books cost?

problem: How much money went to each of the 4 teams? At the school fair, children played 23 games of ring toss in the morning and 17 in the afternoon, each game costing $2, and the takings were split equally among the teams.
follow_up_questions: The red team spends $14. How much does the red team have left?
The blue team spends half its money on medals. What do the medals cost?

problem: Mr. Lee planted 42 tulip bulbs in 6 equal rows. How many bulbs are in each row?
How many books go on each shelf when a librarian spreads 42 new books evenly over 6 shelves?
On Friday a puppet theatre sold 10 tickets for $60 in all, every ticket at the same price. The show was 95 minutes long. What did one ticket cost?
follow_up_questions: On Saturday tickets cost $2 more. What is the new price?
Saturday sells just as many tickets. How much money does the theatre take?

problem: What was the price of one ride? The museum's mini train, whose trip takes 95 seconds, earned $60 from 10 riders who each paid the same.
follow_up_questions: Later the ride costs $2 more. What is the new price?
If the same number of riders come at the new price, what does the ride earn?

problem: Three teams each raised $24 for the gym. With all of it they bought 8 new hula hoops at the same price. What did one hoop cost?
follow_up_questions: A jump rope costs $4 less than a hoop. What does a jump rope cost?
The gym buys 2 jump ropes. What does it pay for them?
How much did the hoops and the jump ropes cost altogether?

problem: What was the price of each new chair? Every one of 3 grades collected $24 for the library, and the total paid for 8 chairs, each costing the same.
follow_up_questions: A cushion costs $4 less than a chair. How much is a cushion?
The library buys 2 cushions. How much do they cost?
What did the chairs and the cushions cost in total?

problem: Ana's new backpack cost $45, and she paid for it in 9 equal payments. It has a pocket shaped like a fox. How much was each payment?
follow_up_questions: A lunch box costs as much as three of those payments. How much does the lunch box cost?

problem: How much was one payment? Felix bought a $45 kite set and paid in 9 equal parts over the summer. The kite looks like a dragon.
follow_up_questions: The kite string costs the same as three payments. What does the string cost?

problem: Twenty-four water balloons were filled and split into 3 equal buckets before the water fight. How many balloons were in each bucket?
follow_up_questions: Each team throws 5 balloons from its bucket. How many are left in one bucket?
How many balloons are left in all the buckets together?

problem: How many pine cones were in each heap? The children gathered 24 pine cones and made 3 equal heaps for a craft.
follow_up_questions: Each group uses 5 cones from its heap. How many cones are left in a heap?
What is the total number of cones left in every heap?

problem: On a cold Saturday, the ice rink took in $84 from six families, and each family paid the same. How much did one family pay?
How much did each club pay? The swimming pool earned $84 from 6 clubs on a windy afternoon, the same amount from every club.
Hiro's art club received 28 tubes of glitter to share equally among its 7 members. The club has met 15 times so far. How many tubes does each member get?
follow_up_questions: Hiro already had 9 tubes at home. How many does he have now?

problem: How many marbles does each child get? A teacher splits 28 marbles evenly among the 7 children sitting at table 15.
follow_up_questions: Pablo had 9 marbles in his pocket already. How many does he have now?

problem: Art class fees are paid over 5 lessons. Bilal paid $25 altogether, the same each lesson. How much did he pay per lesson?
follow_up_questions: Next term there are 8 lessons at the same price. How much will Bilal pay?
His grandma pays $15 of that. How much does Bilal pay himself?

problem: What did Freya pay for each visit? Her climbing gym pass cost $25 for 5 visits, all priced the same.
follow_up_questions: Next month she plans 8 visits at the same price. What will that cost?
A coupon covers $15 of it. How much does Freya still pay?

problem: At the end of the yard sale, the cash box held $36. Mr. Varga paid his 4 helpers equally from it. A dog slept under the table all day. How much did each helper earn?
follow_up_questions: Each helper had worked 3 hours. How much did a helper earn per hour?

problem: How much did each babysitter get? Mrs. Ngata paid $36 to 4 babysitters, sharing it equally. Her baby giggled the whole evening.
follow_up_questions: Each one babysat for 3 hours. What did a babysitter earn each hour?

problem: The choir sold cupcakes, all at the same price. Eight cupcakes brought in $40. What was the price of one cupcake?
What did one dog wash cost if the scouts charged the same for each dog and earned $40 from 8 dogs?
Seven children sold bookmarks at the school fair, taking in $28 altogether, with each child selling the same amount. How much did one child take in?
follow_up_questions: Each bookmark cost $2. How many bookmarks did one child sell?

problem: How much money did each stall make? At the craft market, 7 stalls made $28 in total, all the same amount.
follow_up_questions: Every item at the stalls cost $2. How many items did one stall sell?

problem: A bundle of 5 bus passes costs $40 at the station. What does one pass in the bundle cost?
follow_up_questions: A single pass bought alone costs $10. How much is saved on each pass with the bundle?
How much is saved on the whole bundle?
The savings are spent on sandwiches at $5 each. How many sandwiches is that?

problem: What is the cost of one swim entry on the pool's 5-entry card, which sells for $40?
follow_up_questions: One entry on its own costs $10. What does the card save on each entry?
What is the saving on the whole card?
If that saving buys juice boxes at $5 each, how many juice boxes is that?

problem: Two grades gathered shells for an art project: one grade found 46 and the other found 38. The shells were split equally into 7 jars. The project will be a big fish. How many shells went into each jar?
follow_up_questions: Each jar has shells of 3 sizes in equal numbers. How many shells of each size are in one jar?
The artists use 2 full jars for the fish's tail. How many shells is that?

problem: How many buttons went into each tin? For a quilt, Gran saved 46 buttons and Aunt May saved 38, and they sorted them all equally into 7 tins. The quilt will hang in the hall.
follow_up_questions: In every tin there are buttons of 3 shapes in equal amounts. How many buttons of one shape are in a tin?
Gran uses 2 full tins for the border. How many buttons does she use?

problem: Mr. Osei spent $60 on pool passes for his 3 daughters. Every pass had the same price. How much was one pass?
What did one museum membership cost if Grandma paid $60 for 3 of them, all the same price?
Leaves fell for 8 days straight. Mr. Brandt paid twins Kip and Lars $14 to rake the yard, and both boys share it equally. What does each boy get?
follow_up_questions: Kip spends $3 on a comic. How much does he keep?

problem: How much does each sister get? Their grandfather paid Nia and Zola $14 for weeding his garden, which has 8 rose bushes, and the two sisters share the money equally.
follow_up_questions: Nia spends $3 on seeds. How much money does she have left?

problem: After the match, 4 teammates went for burgers. The bill was $38 and they added a $6 tip, then shared the whole amount equally. How much did each teammate pay?
follow_up_questions: They also shared 12 chicken nuggets evenly. How many nuggets did each teammate eat?

problem: What did each cousin pay? Four cousins took a taxi to the beach: the fare was $38, the tip was $6, and they split the total evenly.
follow_up_questions: They brought 12 sandwiches and shared them equally. How many sandwiches did each cousin get?

problem: Ten scouts rode a minibus to the aquarium. The minibus cost $50, split equally. What was each scout's fare?
follow_up_questions: Aquarium tickets are $7 each. How much did one scout spend on the minibus and the ticket?
How much did all the scouts spend together?

problem: How much did each player pay for the van? The van to the away game cost $50, and the 10 players split it evenly.
follow_up_questions: Each player also buys a $7 lunch. What does one player spend on the van and lunch?
What is the total spent by all the players?

problem: Tomas's club sold 18 bags of popcorn at $3 a bag during a 5 hour game. The 6 club members split the money evenly. What does each member get?
follow_up_questions: Tomas spends his share on corn kernels at $3 a packet. How many packets can he buy?
Each packet makes 6 bowls of popcorn. How many bowls can he make?

problem: What is each child's share? Six children ran a face-painting table for 5 hours and painted 18 faces at $3 each, sharing the money equally.
follow_up_questions: Ella buys paint pots with her share at $3 each. How many pots does she buy?
Each pot paints 6 faces. How many faces can she paint?

problem: Pia's garage sale made $44, and she shared it so that all 4 helpers got the same. How much did each helper get?
follow_up_questions: Pia, one of the helpers, spends $6 of her share on a book. How much does she have left?
Her friend Mo got the same share and spent nothing. How much more does Mo have than Pia?
Mo gives Pia $3. How much does Pia have now?

problem: How much did each of the 4 gardeners receive? The community garden sold vegetables for $44 and split the money evenly.
follow_up_questions: Ravi spends $6 on a trowel. What is left of his share?
Another gardener, June, spent none of hers. How much more money does June have than Ravi?
June gives Ravi $3. What does Ravi have now?

problem: Costumes for the class parade cost $48 and masks cost $12. Three teachers shared the bill equally. How much did each teacher pay?
follow_up_questions: One teacher paid with a $50 note. How much change did she get?
Another teacher paid with three $10 notes. What change did he get?

problem: What did each of the 3 grandparents pay? They shared equally the cost of a $48 tent and a $12 set of pegs.
follow_up_questions: One grandparent used a $50 note. How much change came back?
Another paid with three $10 notes. How much change did that one get?

problem: A garden path divides 36 rose bushes into 4 equal beds. How many bushes are in each bed?
How many lockers are in each row if the 36 lockers in the hallway are arranged in 4 equal rows?
Six juice boxes from the school canteen cost $12. The canteen sells 15 kinds of sandwiches. How much is one juice box?
follow_up_questions: Smoothies cost $1 more than juice boxes. How much would 4 smoothies cost?

problem: What is the price of one pencil if 6 pencils at the stationery shop cost $12? The shop has 15 colours of paper.
follow_up_questions: A pen costs $1 more than a pencil. What do 4 pens cost?

problem: By noon on the first hot day, the beach shop had made $81 from selling 9 umbrellas, all at one price. How much was each umbrella?
follow_up_questions: In the afternoon it sells 4 more umbrellas. How much money do those bring in?
How much did the shop make from umbrellas for the whole day?
The owner spends $17 of it on sunscreen for the shop. How much is left?

problem: What did one pumpkin cost? A farm stand sold 9 pumpkins before lunch, all for the same price, and took in $81.
follow_up_questions: After lunch it sells 4 more. What do those bring in?
What were the pumpkin sales for the whole day?
The farmer pays $17 for straw out of that money. What remains?

problem: On a snowy day, Ayla's family of 6 went to the aquarium, and entry for all of them cost $30. Snow melted from their boots onto the floor. If each person paid the same, what was one person's entry?
follow_up_questions: Watching the dolphin show is $3 more for each person. What does the family pay for the show?

problem: What did one person pay to enter the zoo? The 6 members of the Park family paid $30 altogether, each the same amount. A peacock walked right past the gate.
follow_up_questions: Feeding the giraffes costs $3 per person. What does the family pay so everyone can feed them?

problem: A coach hands out 35 cones equally to 5 groups for a drill. How many cones does each group get?
How many beads go to each child when 35 beads are shared equally among 5 children?
At the market, 5 bunches of flowers sell for $30 in total. What is the price of one bunch?
follow_up_questions: A ribbon costs $1 extra per bunch. What would 3 bunches with ribbons cost?

problem: What does one kite cost? The toy shop charges $30 for 5 kites, all the same price.
follow_up_questions: A long tail adds $1 to the price of each kite. How much would 3 kites with long tails cost?

problem: Sven baked 4 trays of brownies for the school play and sold each tray for the same price, making $32 in total. What did one tray sell for?
follow_up_questions: The ingredients for each tray cost him $5. What profit does he make on one tray?
What is his profit on all the trays?
He wants a $20 kite. How much more does he need?

problem: How much did one birdhouse sell for? Nell built 4 birdhouses and sold them all at the same price for $32 altogether.
follow_up_questions: Wood and nails for each birdhouse cost $5. What profit does she make on one?
What profit does she make on all of them?
She is saving for a $20 hammer. How much more money does she need?

problem: To pay for new jerseys, the 9 members of a volleyball team sold hot dogs. They charged $5 each and sold 18 hot dogs. A seagull stole a bun from the table. If the money is shared equally, how much does each member get?
follow_up_questions: Wristbands cost $4 each. How much does each member have left after buying one?
The coach doubles each member's leftover money. How much does a member have now?

problem: How much does each of the 9 dancers get? Their troupe washed 18 cars at $5 per car to raise money for costumes, and they share the money equally. The soap bucket kept tipping over.
follow_up_questions: Each dancer buys a $4 pair of tights. How much does each dancer have left?
Their teacher doubles each dancer's leftover money. How much does a dancer have now?

problem: Aunt Sofia took her 3 nephews to the circus and paid $27 for their tickets. What did each nephew's ticket cost?
What was the price of one ticket? Grandma Rui spent $27 on puppet show tickets for her 3 grandchildren.
In the school library, 56 books stand evenly on 8 shelves. The library has 5 computers. How many books are on one shelf?
follow_up_questions: Lena borrows 3 books from one shelf. How many books remain on that shelf?

problem: How many jars sit on each shelf of the pantry? There are 56 jars spread evenly over 8 shelves, and the pantry door has 5 hooks.
follow_up_questions: Dad takes 3 jars off one shelf for cooking. How many are still on that shelf?

problem: Owen spent $60 on 4 museum tickets and 4 sandwiches. Each sandwich cost $3, and the tickets were all the same price. What did one ticket cost?
follow_up_questions: Next month he buys just 2 tickets and no sandwiches. How much does he pay?

problem: What is the price of one entry ticket? At the theme park, Leila paid $60 for 4 entry tickets plus 4 ice creams at $3 each, and every ticket cost the same.
follow_up_questions: On her next visit she buys only 2 entry tickets. What does she pay?

problem: The garden club spent $36 on 4 watering cans, all the same price. What did one watering can cost?
follow_up_questions: A trowel costs $4 less than a watering can. How much is a trowel?
How much do 6 trowels cost?

problem: How much was one lamp? A hotel spent $36 buying 4 desk lamps, each costing the same.
follow_up_questions: A light bulb costs $4 less than a lamp. What does a bulb cost?
What do 6 bulbs cost?

problem: A $48 tent was bought for a camping trip, and 6 friends shared the cost evenly. What did each friend pay?
follow_up_questions: If 8 friends had shared the cost instead, how much would each have paid?

problem: What does each family pay? Six families split the $48 cost of a bouncy castle for the street party equally.
follow_up_questions: Suppose 8 families had shared it instead. What would each family pay?

problem: Marta had 20 candles and put the same number on each of her 4 cakes. How many candles were on one cake?
How many stickers did each notebook get? Jalen had 20 stickers and stuck an equal number on each of his 4 notebooks.
During a 4 day holiday, the Ortiz kids made friendship bracelets and sold 27 of them at $2 each. The 3 kids split the money evenly. How much did each kid get?
follow_up_questions: Each kid puts half of the share in a piggy bank. How much does one kid put in?
How much do all the kids put in their piggy banks together?

problem: How much money does each of the 3 Abbott children get? They sold 27 cups of cocoa at $2 a cup during a snowstorm that lasted 4 hours and shared the money evenly.
follow_up_questions: Each child saves half of the money. How much does one child save?
What do all the children save altogether?

problem: A box of 6 paintbrushes sells for $18 at the art shop. How much is each paintbrush?
follow_up_questions: Ella needs a brush for each of her 4 paint sets. How much will she pay?
She pays with a $20 note. What change does she get?
With her change she buys erasers at $2 each. How many erasers can she buy?

problem: How much is one tennis ball, if a tube of 6 balls costs $18?
follow_up_questions: Coach Ray needs 4 balls for practice. How much will he pay?
He hands over a $20 note. What is his change?
He spends the change on wristbands at $2 each. How many wristbands does he get?

problem: Seeds, soil and pots cost the garden club $63, the same amount for each of its 7 flower beds. Everyone chose sunflowers as the club flower. How much was spent on each bed?
follow_up_questions: One bed needed an extra $4 bag of compost. How much was spent on that bed altogether?

problem: How much did each costume cost? The drama class spent $63 on fabric, buttons and thread, the same amount for each of its 7 costumes. The stage curtain is dark red.
follow_up_questions: One costume needed an extra $4 hat. What was spent on that costume in total?

problem: Coach Diaz bought 8 water bottles for the team and paid with two $20 notes. She got $8 back. Every bottle cost the same. How much was one bottle?
follow_up_questions: A bottle with a straw lid costs $1 more. What would the 8 bottles have cost with straw lids?
How much more would the straw-lid bottles cost than the plain ones?

problem: What was the price of one sandwich? Mr. Kaya ordered 8 sandwiches for a picnic, handed over two $20 notes, and received $8 in change; all the sandwiches cost the same.
follow_up_questions: Adding cheese costs $1 more per sandwich. What would the 8 sandwiches have cost with cheese?
By how much is the cheese order more expensive than the plain sandwiches?

problem: Leah's tin now holds $35. She filled it by adding the same number of dollars from dog walking on each day of one week. How many dollars did she add per day?
How many pages did Omar read each day if he finished a 35-page comic in a week, reading the same number every day?
By lunchtime, the choir had sold 7 bags of cookies and had $28 in the tin, and 12 trays had been emptied. Every bag cost the same. What was the price of one bag?
follow_up_questions: In the afternoon they sold 9 more bags. How much did those bags bring in?

problem: What did each bike repair cost? Before noon, a repair stall fixed 7 bikes and collected $28, all at the same price, and used 12 patches.
follow_up_questions: After noon it fixed 9 more bikes. How much money did those bring in?

problem: Two trains each brought 48 fans to the stadium. Inside, the fans were split evenly among 8 sections. How many fans were in each section?
follow_up_questions: In each section, 5 fans wear hats. How many fans in a section have no hat?
How many fans without hats are there across all the sections?

problem: How many campers slept in each cabin? Two vans each carried 48 campers to the lake, and the campers were shared equally among 8 cabins.
follow_up_questions: In every cabin, 5 campers are new. How many campers in a cabin have been before?
Across all the cabins, how many campers have been before?

problem: The garden club had $45 in gifts for the spring planting. It set aside the same amount for each of its 5 flower beds. How much was set aside per bed?
follow_up_questions: The first bed uses only $6. How much of its money is left?
That leftover money goes to the last bed. How much can the last bed spend?
The last bed spends all of its money on bulbs at $4 a bag. How many bags is that?

problem: How much was each class trip's budget? A school received $45 from parents and split it equally among 5 class trips.
follow_up_questions: One trip spends only $6. How much of its budget is unused?
The unused money is added to the final trip's budget. What can the final trip spend?
The final trip spends everything on snacks at $4 a box. How many boxes is that?

problem: Nora's pocket money, $20, all went on 4 sticker packs at the fair, each costing the same. The fair had a giant Ferris wheel. Find the price of one sticker pack.
follow_up_questions: Her brother bought 2 of the same packs. What did he pay?

problem: What did one comic cost? Kai spent his $20 gift exactly on 4 comics with equal prices. The shop smelled of old paper.
follow_up_questions: His friend bought 2 of the same comics. How much did his friend pay?

problem: The coach splits 18 swimmers evenly across 3 lanes. How many swimmers are in each lane?
How many ducks are in each pond if 18 ducks share 3 ponds equally?
A canoe trip cost $85 and life jacket rental cost $15. The lake has 11 islands. The 5 campers split the full cost evenly. How much did each camper pay?
follow_up_questions: Mara, one of the campers, had brought $32. How much does she have left?
She spends a third of what is left on a postcard. How much does the postcard cost?

problem: How much did each climber pay? At a cliff that is 11 metres high, a group of 5 climbers split evenly the $85 guide fee and $15 for rope hire.
follow_up_questions: Jun had $32 in his wallet. What does he have after paying?
He spends a third of what is left on lunch. What does lunch cost?

problem: On a snowy afternoon, Rafa divided his 30 marbles equally into 5 bags for his friends. How many marbles were in each bag?
follow_up_questions: Each friend loses 2 marbles. How many are left in one bag?
How many marbles are left in all the bags?
Rafa adds a new bag of 12 marbles. How many marbles are there now?

problem: How many pencils went into each pencil case? Ms. Ito shared 30 new pencils equally among 5 cases for her art group.
follow_up_questions: Each case loses 2 pencils by Friday. How many pencils are left in one case?
How many pencils are left in all the cases together?
She adds a fresh box of 12 pencils. What is the total number of pencils now?

problem: To pay for science fair projects, the class sold 25 cupcakes at $3 each. The cupcakes had green frosting. The money will be shared equally among 5 projects. How much will each project get?
follow_up_questions: The volcano project needs $25. How much more does it need beyond its share?
Two students cover that gap equally. How much does each student give?

problem: How much money will each of the 5 animal shelters receive? Students sold 25 painted rocks at $3 apiece and will divide the money equally among the shelters. The rocks were painted with ladybugs.
follow_up_questions: The cat shelter needs $25 for a new bed. How much more does it need than its share?
Two teachers split that gap evenly. How much does each teacher give?

problem: Zoe has a bracelet kit with 24 beads. She puts them into 8 cups, the same number in each. How many beads are in one cup?
How many pencils are in each pot when a teacher shares 24 pencils equally among 8 pots?
When the bakery closed, its 5 bakers counted $35 in the tip jar. They had baked 60 loaves that day. If they share the tips equally, how much does each baker get?
follow_up_questions: One baker adds his share to the $13 he saved last week. What is his total now?

problem: How much does each lifeguard get? At the end of the day, after 60 swimmers had visited, the 5 lifeguards at the pool found $35 in a tip box and shared it equally.
follow_up_questions: One lifeguard puts her share with $13 she already had. How much does she have now?

problem: A bake sale raised $60, which was split equally among 3 groups: a zoo, a park club and a museum. What was each group's share?
follow_up_questions: The museum uses its share to buy 4 posters at the same price. How much does each poster cost?
The zoo gets $15 more from another donor. How much does it have now?

problem: What did each of the 3 schools get? The town fun run raised $60 and divided it equally among the schools.
follow_up_questions: One school buys 4 footballs with its share, all at one price. What does one football cost?
Another school adds $15 from a cake sale to its share. What does it have now?

problem: Mr. Bauer wants his class to read 42 short stories before the holidays. There are 6 days left, and the class will read the same number each day. How many stories should they read each day?
follow_up_questions: On the last day the class reads 3 extra stories for fun. How many stories do they read that day?

problem: How many push-ups should Aditi do each day? Before her sports test she wants to do 42 push-ups over the next 6 days, the same amount daily.
follow_up_questions: On the final day she feels strong and does 3 extra. How many push-ups does she do that day?

problem: Nine campers are getting ready for a canoe trip that leaves at 14 minutes past eight. They have 36 apples to carry, shared evenly among them. How many apples go in each camper's bag?
follow_up_questions: By noon each camper has eaten 2 apples. How many apples does each camper still carry?
How many apples are left in all nine bags together?

problem: How many juice boxes does each child carry? Before the 14 km bike ride, the 9 riders share 36 juice boxes equally.
follow_up_questions: At the halfway stop, each rider drinks 2 juice boxes. How many does each rider have left?
How many juice boxes are left among all the riders?

problem: On Saturday the library received 38 boxes of donated books, and on Sunday it received 34 more. Volunteers will shelve all the boxes over the next 8 evenings, the same number each evening. How many boxes will they shelve each evening?

How many crates will the packers load each hour? A farm picked 38 crates of peaches in the morning and 34 crates in the afternoon, and the packers will load them all onto trucks over 8 hours at an even pace.
A delivery driver has 45 boxes of fruit to drop at 5 shops, the same number at each shop. How many boxes does each shop get?
follow_up_questions: At every shop she also collects 12 empty crates. How many crates does she collect?
Back at the farm, she stacks the crates equally into 6 piles. How many crates are in each pile?
She loads 3 of the piles onto a truck before lunch. How many crates are still waiting after that?

problem: How many newspapers does Oskar leave on each street? He has 45 newspapers and 5 streets on his route, and every street gets the same number.
follow_up_questions: On each street he also collects 12 old newspapers for recycling. How many does he collect?
He bundles those old papers into 6 equal stacks. How many papers are in each stack?
He drops 3 stacks at the recycling bin. How many old papers are still with him?

problem: A school orders 4 packs of 24 glue sticks. The secretary shares them equally among the 6 classrooms. How many glue sticks does each classroom get?
follow_up_questions: By June each classroom has used 9 glue sticks. How many are left in each classroom?
How many unused glue sticks are there in all the classrooms?

problem: How many tennis balls does each court get? The club buys 4 bags with 24 balls in each and splits them evenly among its 6 courts.
follow_up_questions: Over the week, each court loses 9 balls. How many balls remain at each court?
In all, how many balls remain at the courts?

problem: For the library's reading day, the librarian divided 32 bookmarks evenly into 4 boxes. The library has 3 floors. How many bookmarks go into each box?
follow_up_questions: Before the doors open, each box gets 5 more bookmarks. How many bookmarks are in a box now?

problem: How many badges are in each bowl? Beside the 3 penguin pools, the zookeepers sort 32 animal badges equally into 4 bowls for visitors.
follow_up_questions: Each bowl is topped up with 5 extra badges. How many badges does a bowl hold now?

problem: A farmer plants 63 rows of beans in a week, planting the same number of rows on each of the 7 days. How many rows does she plant each day?
How many pages must Tomas write each day? His story needs 63 pages and he has 7 days to finish, writing an equal number daily.
Before the cafe opens, Rhea puts 40 cupcakes on 5 plates, the same number on each plate. How many cupcakes are on one plate?
follow_up_questions: A customer buys 2 plates of cupcakes. How many cupcakes does the customer get?

problem: How many fish are in each tank? At the pet shop, Mr. Adeyemi places 40 goldfish into 5 tanks, an equal number in every tank, before the shop opens at nine.
follow_up_questions: A family buys all the fish in 2 tanks. How many goldfish did they buy?

problem: The flower show lasts 6 days, and 54 rose bushes must be judged. Each bush has 8 blooms. If the judges look at the same number of bushes every day, how many bushes do they judge per day?
follow_up_questions: On the first day, 2 of that day's bushes are taken away before judging. How many bushes are judged that day?
Each of the 3 judges writes a note for every bush judged that day. How many notes are written on the first day?

problem: How many paintings does the art panel judge each day? The art contest has 54 paintings, each using 8 colours, and judging takes 6 days with an equal number per day.
follow_up_questions: On day one, 2 of the day's paintings arrive late and are not judged. How many are judged that day?
There are 3 judges, and each gives a score to every painting judged that day. How many scores are given on day one?

problem: The art teacher buys 3 boxes of 32 crayons each. She shares them all equally among the class's 8 tables before Friday's lesson. How many new crayons go to each table?
How many seeds does each pot get? Gardener Wanjiru opens 3 packets with 32 seeds in each and divides all of them equally among 8 pots.
On Monday, 5 teams collected 85 bottles for the recycling bin, each team the same number. How many bottles did each team collect?
follow_up_questions: On Tuesday, the blue team collected 6 more than it did on Monday. How many did the blue team collect on Tuesday?
How many bottles did the blue team collect over the two days?

problem: How many cans did each family donate? At the food drive, 85 cans came from 5 families, every family giving the same number.
follow_up_questions: The next month, the Rossi family gave 6 more cans than before. How many cans did they give?
Altogether, how many cans did the Rossi family give in the two months?

problem: A school pantry has 75 boxes of pasta and 21 boxes of cereal. On Friday, the staff share all the boxes equally among 8 classrooms. How many boxes does each classroom get?
follow_up_questions: Each box weighs 2 kilograms. How many kilograms does one classroom receive?

problem: How many sacks does each farm get? The co-op has 75 sacks of seed and 21 sacks of fertiliser and splits all of them evenly among 8 farms.
follow_up_questions: Every sack weighs 2 kilograms. What weight does one farm receive?

problem: The school fair lasts 3 days, and a stall has 81 balloons. Mrs. Haas, one of the stall's 4 helpers, blows up the same number each day so they last the whole fair. How many balloons does she blow up each day?
follow_up_questions: On the first day she sells all but 5 of them. How many did she sell?
Each balloon costs 2 dollars. How much money did those sales bring in?
She shares that money equally among 4 jars. How much goes in each jar?

problem: How many jars of jam does Mr. Obi put on his table each day? The market runs for 3 days, he has 81 jars, and he sets out an equal number daily; his stand has 4 umbrellas.
follow_up_questions: On day one he sells all but 5 of the jars he set out. How many jars did he sell?
Every jar sells for 2 dollars. How much did he earn from those jars?
He divides the money equally into 4 pouches. How much is in each pouch?

problem: A hairdresser gives 24 haircuts on Saturday, the same number in each of the 4 hours the salon is open. The salon has a parrot that says hello. How many haircuts does she give each hour?
How many cars does the mechanic fix each hour? Over the 4 hours her garage opens on Sunday, she fixes 24 cars, the same number every hour. The garage smells of oil.
This month the zoo keepers must clean each of the 2 elephant pools 14 times. The cleanings are spread evenly over 4 weeks. How many pool cleanings happen each week?
follow_up_questions: Each cleaning takes 15 minutes. How many minutes of cleaning is that in one week?
If 3 keepers share that time equally, how many minutes does each keeper spend cleaning?

problem: How many polishes happen each week? A museum must polish each of its 2 statues 14 times this month, spreading the work evenly across 4 weeks.
follow_up_questions: One polish takes 15 minutes. How many minutes of polishing happen in a week?
The work is shared equally among 3 guards. How many minutes does each guard polish?

problem: A gardener has 48 hedge plants to put in by Friday. She wants to plant the same number on each of the 4 days from Tuesday to Friday. How many plants must she put in each day?
follow_up_questions: On Tuesday, a storm stops her after only 7 plants. How many of Tuesday's plants are still not in the ground?

problem: How many tiles must the workers lay each day? The new swimming pool needs 48 tiles laid, spread equally over 4 workdays.
follow_up_questions: On the first workday, the glue runs out after only 7 tiles. How many of that day's tiles are left to lay?

problem: Across one week, from Monday to Sunday, Ruth baked 35 loaves of bread at her shop, the same number each day. How many loaves did she bake on Thursday?
follow_up_questions: Each loaf sells for 8 dollars. How much money do Thursday's loaves bring in?

problem: How many shoes did the cobbler mend on Friday? Over a full week he mended 35 shoes, the same number every day.
follow_up_questions: He charges 8 dollars for each shoe. What did he earn on Friday?

problem: Kamal must set up his fruit stand by 10 on Saturday morning. First he divides 72 oranges evenly among 8 crates. How many oranges are in each crate?
follow_up_questions: By noon, 3 crates are empty because all their oranges sold. How many oranges were sold?
How many oranges are still in crates?

problem: How many cupcakes go on each tray? Before the bake sale opens at 10, Nina spreads 72 cupcakes evenly over 8 trays.
follow_up_questions: By lunch, 3 trays are sold out. How many cupcakes were sold?
How many cupcakes are still left on trays?

problem: An orchard has 5 rows with 18 apple trees in each row. The owner, Mr. Silva, plans to prune them in 6 equal groups, one group each weekend. How many trees are in each group?
How many chairs go in each classroom? The hall has 5 stacks of 18 chairs, and the caretaker will move all of them into 6 classrooms in equal numbers.
The students have 72 paper lanterns to hang in the school hall over 4 afternoons, the same number each afternoon. The hall floor was just polished. How many lanterns do they hang each afternoon?
follow_up_questions: On the second afternoon, 6 of that afternoon's lanterns fall down. How many of them are still hanging?

problem: How many posters go up each day? The town council will put up 72 posters for the festival over 4 days, an equal number each day. The festival has a dragon parade.
follow_up_questions: On the second day, rain ruins 6 of that day's posters. How many of that day's posters are still fine?

problem: Sixty-four puzzle pieces were found under the sofa. Luis sorts them into 4 equal piles. How many pieces are in each pile?
follow_up_questions: A whole puzzle has 32 pieces. How many piles make up one whole puzzle?
In every pile, 3 pieces are bent, and he throws them out. How many good pieces are left in one pile?
How many good pieces are left in all the piles together?

problem: How many cards are in each stack? Mei found 64 playing cards in a drawer and dealt them into 4 equal stacks.
follow_up_questions: One full deck in her game has 32 cards. How many stacks make one full deck?
She finds 3 torn cards in each stack and removes them. How many good cards are left in a stack?
How many good cards remain across all the stacks?

problem: Students collected 46 books on Monday and 50 on Tuesday. On Wednesday they packed all the books into 6 boxes, the same number in every box. How many books were in each box?
follow_up_questions: Before sending, 4 damaged books are taken out of each box. How many good books are in each box?
Each box goes to a different school. How many good books do the schools get in total?

problem: How many toys went into each sack? A toy drive got 46 toys from one street and 50 from another, and volunteers divided all of them equally into 6 sacks.
follow_up_questions: Then 4 broken toys are removed from each sack. How many good toys are in each sack?
Each sack goes to a different hospital. How many good toys do the hospitals get altogether?

problem: A book drive lasts 5 days. Ms. Torres's class, which has 19 desks, promises to collect 55 books in that time, the same number each day. How many books should the class collect each day?
follow_up_questions: On the last day the class collects 2 more books than planned. How many does it collect that day?

problem: How many laps should Ivo swim each day? Over 5 days he wants to swim 55 laps, the same amount daily, in a pool with 19 lockers.
follow_up_questions: On the final day he swims 2 laps more than planned. How many laps does he swim that day?

problem: The farm crew divides 70 eggs equally into 10 cartons. How many eggs are in each carton?
Ten classes visit the library, and the librarian hands out 70 bookmarks equally among them. How many bookmarks does each class get?
The bakery made 98 rolls in the morning and 2 more in the afternoon. In the evening, a baker named Rosa packs them equally into 5 boxes, one for each cafe. How many rolls go in each box?
follow_up_questions: In the box for the corner cafe, 7 rolls are burnt. How many rolls in that box are good?
Fresh rolls cost 2 dollars each to replace. How much will replacing the burnt rolls cost?

problem: How many marbles are in each jar? Tariq has 98 marbles and finds 2 more under his bed, then shares them all equally among 5 jars.
follow_up_questions: In the red jar, 7 marbles are cracked. How many marbles in that jar are not cracked?
New marbles cost 2 dollars each. How much will it cost to replace the cracked ones?

problem: A vet checks 66 puppies over 3 mornings, the same number each morning. How many puppies does she check each morning?
follow_up_questions: One helper can bathe 11 puppies in a morning. How many helpers are needed each morning?

problem: How many sandwiches are made each day? The camp cook has 66 sandwiches to make over 3 days, an equal number daily.
follow_up_questions: One cook can make 11 sandwiches a day. How many cooks are needed each day?

problem: Officer Grant has 5 school talks this month. She brings 50 sticker badges and gives away the same number at each talk. The children always want to see her police car. How many badges does she give away at each talk?
follow_up_questions: At the first school there are 4 more children than badges. How many children are there?
Each child also gets 2 safety leaflets. How many leaflets does she give out at the first school?
She started with 40 leaflets. How many are left after the first school?

problem: How many seed packets does the gardener hand out at each fair? Mr. Novak visits 5 garden fairs and takes 50 seed packets, giving away an equal number at each fair. He wears a straw hat everywhere.
follow_up_questions: At the first fair, 4 more people come than there are packets. How many people come?
Each person also gets 2 plant labels. How many labels does he hand out at that fair?
He brought 40 labels. How many does he have left after the first fair?

problem: The farm's tractor is 25 years old. It moves 36 hay bales over 4 days, the same number each day. How many bales does it move each day?
follow_up_questions: Each bale takes 5 minutes to move. How many minutes does the tractor spend moving bales in a day?
The tractor starts 15 minutes after the farmer wakes up. How many minutes after the farmer wakes up does it finish?

problem: How many boxes does the forklift carry each day? In a warehouse whose roof is 25 metres high, it carries 36 boxes over 4 days, the same number daily.
follow_up_questions: Every box takes 5 minutes. How many minutes of carrying is that in one day?
The forklift starts 15 minutes after the gates open. How many minutes after the gates open does it finish?

problem: Before the holidays, a toy workshop needs to make 84 wooden trains. Its 3 carvers will each make the same number, spread evenly over 4 days. How many trains does one carver make per day?
How many scarves does each knitter finish per day? A club must knit 84 scarves for winter; 3 knitters share the work equally, and each spreads her part evenly over 4 days.
At the end of the market, the 4 stall holders share the 28 leftover melons equally. How many melons does each stall holder take?
follow_up_questions: One of them, Hamid, gives 3 of his to a neighbour. How many does he have left?
Hamid cuts each remaining melon into 2 pieces. How many pieces does he have?

problem: How many plants does each teacher take home? At the end of the school year, the 4 teachers share the 28 leftover potted plants equally.
follow_up_questions: Ms. Dube gives 3 of hers to a friend. How many plants does she have left?
She waters each remaining plant with 2 cups of water. How many cups does she use?

problem: At the fun fair, the bumper cars gave 37 rides before noon and 44 after noon. The 9 cars were used equally, so each car gave the same number of rides. How many rides did each car give?
follow_up_questions: Each ride lasts 5 minutes. How many minutes was each car in use?

problem: How many tours did each guide lead? The castle had 37 tours in the morning and 44 in the afternoon, shared equally by 9 guides.
follow_up_questions: Each tour lasts 5 minutes. How many minutes did each guide spend leading tours?

problem: Ms. Park has 18 science kits for her class's 3 lab teams, which meet at 4 o'clock. If she shares the kits equally among the teams, how many kits does each team get?
follow_up_questions: Each team uses its kits over 2 weeks, the same number each week. How many kits does a team use per week?
Every kit has 5 experiments. How many experiments does a team do in a week?
The team shares those experiments evenly among its 3 members. How many experiments does each member do per week?

problem: How many puzzles does each reading group get? The librarian splits 18 puzzles equally among 3 groups that meet in a room with 4 windows.
follow_up_questions: Each group finishes its puzzles over 2 weeks, the same number per week. How many puzzles does a group finish each week?
Each puzzle has 5 levels. How many levels does a group finish in a week?
The levels are shared equally among the group's 3 children. How many levels does each child finish per week?

problem: At the beach party, the lifeguard, Nadia, shares 45 grapes equally among 9 children sitting on a blanket. The waves are loud and foamy. How many grapes does each child get?
How many stickers does each player get? After the final match, Coach Ben gives out 45 stickers equally to the 9 players on his team. The grass is still wet from the rain.
There are 90 bottles of water at the sports camp on Saturday. The organiser, Mrs. Chen, plans to hand them out equally over 3 days. How many bottles will go out each day?
follow_up_questions: On the first day, 24 bottles are handed out in the morning. How many of that day's bottles are left for the afternoon?

problem: How many blankets will go out each night? The shelter has 90 blankets, and Mr. Ruiz will give them out equally over 3 nights.
follow_up_questions: On the first night, 24 blankets go out before eight. How many of that night's blankets are left for later?

problem: A box of 40 pencils is bought by 8 friends, who share them out equally. How many pencils does each friend get?
follow_up_questions: Each friend uses 2 pencils by the end of the week. How many pencils does each friend have left?

problem: How many seeds does each gardener get? The 8 gardeners on Elm Street split a packet of 40 sunflower seeds equally.
follow_up_questions: Each gardener plants 2 seeds today. How many seeds does each gardener still have?

problem: Before 9 o'clock, the librarian, Mr. Koh, spreads 24 picture books evenly across 3 reading mats. How many books go on each mat?
follow_up_questions: During the morning, children take 4 books from one mat. How many are left on that mat?
Mr. Koh then adds 6 new books to that mat. How many books are on it now?

problem: How many cushions are on each bench? A hotel worker places 24 cushions evenly on the 3 lobby benches, and the lobby has 9 plants.
follow_up_questions: Guests carry off 4 cushions from one bench. How many remain on that bench?
The worker brings 6 more cushions to that bench. How many does it have now?

problem: The cleaners have to wash 56 windows in the school and 49 in the gym. They plan to wash the same number each day for a week. How many windows do they wash each day?
How many trees are planted each day? Over one week, volunteers will plant 56 oak trees and 49 maple trees, the same total number every day.

The new playground is nearly ready, and the benches come next. The workers will put in all 32 benches over the next 8 days, the same number each day. The foreman whistles while he works. How many benches go in each day?
follow_up_questions: Each bench needs 6 bolts. How many bolts are used in one day?

problem: How many shelves does the carpenter fit per day? He has 32 shelves to fit in the new library over 8 days, the same number daily. His toolbox is painted red.
follow_up_questions: Every shelf needs 6 nails. How many nails does he use in a day?

problem: Mario runs a boat rental. Before opening he hangs his 30 life jackets on 5 hooks, the same number on each. How many life jackets are on one hook?
follow_up_questions: By noon, renters have taken 4 life jackets from one hook. How many are left on that hook?
Renters take the same number from each of the other hooks too. How many life jackets have been taken altogether?
Each life jacket rental costs 3 dollars. How much money did those rentals bring in?

problem: How many pairs of skates sit on each rack? Before the rink opens, Freja places 30 pairs of skates on 5 racks, an equal number per rack.
follow_up_questions: Skaters take 4 pairs from one rack. How many pairs are left on that rack?
The same number are taken from every other rack as well. How many pairs have been taken in total?
Renting a pair costs 3 dollars. How much did those rentals earn?

problem: Baker Tobias fills 8 trays with 9 cookies each on Friday night. On Saturday he packs all the cookies into 6 boxes of equal size. How many cookies are in each box?
follow_up_questions: He sells 4 boxes before lunch. How many cookies has he sold?
How many cookies are still unsold?

problem: How many crayons are in each set? A teacher has 8 cups holding 9 crayons each, and she regroups all the crayons into 6 equal sets.
follow_up_questions: She gives 4 sets to the first table. How many crayons is that?
How many crayons does she still have?

problem: Three friends collect 36 shells on Sunday morning and share them equally. The beach has 15 lifeguard towers. How many shells does each friend take home?
follow_up_questions: Each friend paints 5 of their shells. How many of one friend's shells are not painted?

problem: How many eggs does each brother get? On the farm, which has 15 hens, three brothers collect 36 eggs and divide them evenly.
follow_up_questions: Each brother uses 5 of his eggs to bake a cake. How many of one brother's eggs are left?

problem: The tennis club planned 48 matches for its summer league and added 24 more when new players joined. The matches will be played over 8 Saturdays, the same number each Saturday. How many matches are played each Saturday?
follow_up_questions: Each match lasts about 30 minutes. How many minutes of tennis are played on one Saturday?
If 3 matches are played at the same time on different courts, how many minutes does a Saturday's tennis last?

problem: How many concerts happen each Friday? The music school scheduled 48 concerts for the year, then added 24 more, and they will take place over 8 Fridays with the same number each Friday.
follow_up_questions: Each concert lasts 30 minutes. How many minutes of music are there on one Friday?
If 3 concerts run at the same time in different halls, how long does a Friday's music last?

problem: The sports club has 42 medals to give out at the awards night. Each of the 7 teams gets the same number. How many medals does each team receive?
follow_up_questions: One team has 3 players who share their medals equally. How many medals does each of those players get?

problem: How many apples does each basket get? A farmer sorts 42 apples into 7 baskets so every basket has an equal share.
follow_up_questions: One basket is shared equally among 3 children. How many apples does each child get?

problem: The book van visits the school twice a week. Last week the students returned 18 boxes of books, and the van took the same number on each visit. The van has a picture of an owl on it. How many boxes did the van take per visit?
follow_up_questions: Each box holds 7 books. How many books did one visit take away?
This week the students hope to return 6 more boxes than last week. How many boxes is that?
If the van still comes twice, how many boxes will it take per visit this week?

problem: How many sacks did the farmer's truck carry per trip? The truck goes to the mill twice a week, and last week it carried 18 sacks of grain, the same number each trip. The truck's horn is very loud.
follow_up_questions: Every sack weighs 7 kilograms. How many kilograms did one trip carry?
This week the farmer plans to send 6 more sacks than last week. How many sacks is that?
If the truck still makes the trip twice, how many sacks will it carry per trip this week?
